identity: A multiple-choice and true/false question bank from a primary-school Arabic science course (ecosystems, biodiversity, classification, animal life cycles, properties of matter). It is not prose. Question numbers and option letters were never captured, punctuation is stripped, and every <NL> delimits exactly one question block: 20 blocks, 17 of them four-option items and 3 (blocks 11, 15, 19) true/false items closing on [العبارة صحيحة العبارة خاطئة]. The scan is OCR-noisy: عد for عدد at @0, [براد على] for بناء على at @48, الحبة for الحية at @175, and a bare standalone و token at @78 and @81.
law: Exam genre, so the native unit is declared by the genre, not by syntax (doctrine 0e/I1): THE STEM IS ONE UNIT AND EVERY OPTION IS ONE UNIT. Two cuts follow. (a) The stem ends where the options begin, even mid-phrase and even after a dangling copula or preposition (I2). (b) Every option is its own unit whether it runs one word or six, and the short-tail brake is suspended between options (I3). The option run is detected by 3-4 consecutive constituents of the same syntactic type with no connective between them (I4). Symmetrically, the prose connective laws are suspended INSIDE a stem: a stem stays one unit however many clauses or و-conjuncts it holds, so و + new predication and asyndetic finite clauses do not cut there. A و prefixed to a word inside an option is bare-noun و and never cuts (I5).
reasoning: (1) Granularity before syntax. This is the genre that cost me 42 F1 in batch 1 by being read as prose, and my prior runs 7:1 toward under-segmenting, so the failure mode to guard is merging. The <NL>s hand me the block structure free; the work is the ~77 boundaries inside the blocks. (2) Stem-ends. Most are trivial because a four-sibling option run follows. The instructive one is @144: the stem [مقدار المادة التي يحتوي عليها الجسم هو] ends on a dangling copula هو, which is the I2 colon-in-disguise, structurally identical to the batch-1 gold [العام الذي ولد فيه الملك عبدالله الأول ... هو || 1882 م]. The cut goes AFTER هو, not before it. (3) الآتية does NOT take the colon cut here. Six stems carry it (@32, @114, @191, @223, @299, @328) and in every one the announcer is followed by the stem own predicate (ينتج، تعد، يعد، ليست، يوجد) or, at @114, by an inline apposition [البطريق واللقلق] which the stem then governs with [في المجموعة]. The H1 colon cut fires only when the stem ENDS at the announcer; the controlling precedent for bare terms riding inside a sentence that continues is J5 ([معنى المفردات الآتية البيئة الطقس الأوزون], no cuts). So the boundary sits at the end of the predicate, never at الآتية. (4) @11 is the hardest stem-end. [عد أفراد النوع الواحد من الكائنات الحية التي تعيش في نظام بيئي] could be read with a dangling في at @9 and [نظام بيئي] as option 1, giving five options. I reject that: the other candidates ([علاقات غذائية]، [جماعة حيوية]، تنافس، [مجتمع حيوي]) are not fillers for تعيش في, they are the answer set for what a one-species head-count is CALLED, and stopping at @11 yields exactly four. The twin stem at @20 ([عدد الحواس في جسم الإنسان]) confirms both the عد=عدد reading and that في-phrases stay inside these stems. Note @11 is a boundary under either reading, so my only exposure is a possible missed cut at @9, which I accept. Same structure at @118, a boundary whether or not the stem stopped at في. (5) Block 10 (@151-@167) is a two-clause stem: [كتب على زجاجة ماء ٣٥٠ مل] then [على أي الخصائص الفيزيائية تدل هذه الجملة]. Asyndetic finite clauses, which prose doctrine 0f would cut. The native-unit law overrides it (0e), and 0d agrees: [هذه الجملة] is anaphoric to the first clause, so the second refers back rather than advancing. One stem, one unit, cut only at @163. This is 0d used legally under my own section 3.5 restriction: it cancels a cut I was already inclined to make, it does not invent a merge I had never considered. (6) Block 5 (@64-@91) is the only genuinely uncertain site. After the stem [كيف نحافظ على صحتنا] come three asyndetic options ([تجنب الانفعالات] | [التحكم بالمشاعر] | [بناء علاقات ودية وتقبل الرأي الآخر]), then the SAME three repeated at @78-@89 with a standalone و in front of the first two, then [تناول الأدوية]. Reading (a): @78-@89 is one compound all-of-the-above option, so no cut at @80 or @83. Reading (b): it is a duplicated option block, so both cut. I take (b) on three grounds. First, this document already writes all-of-the-above the standard way, [جميع ما ذكر] at @292, so it has no need to spell one out longhand. Second, orthography: every و genuinely internal to an option here is prefixed to its word (والحيوانات، والتربة، وتقبل), whereas @78 and @81 are standalone و tokens, which is what a line-initial و looks like after OCR. Third, @83/@84 is the identical token juncture (بالمشاعر | بناء) to @71/@72, where I cut with high confidence; segmenting the same juncture two ways inside one block needs a reason I do not have. Both marked med. (7) Internal و never cuts. [النباتات والحيوانات الحيوانات والتربة النباتات والهواء الحيوانات والماء] at @210-@217 is FOUR options, not eight. Stem-internal و likewise stays: [وحيد القرن والطيور] at @130, وتنتج at @100 (coordinated under أن), ومكونات at @257. The prose law و + own predication = CUT does not reach inside an exam stem. (8) True/false blocks 11, 15, 19: [العبارة صحيحة] and [العبارة خاطئة] are two exchangeable answer siblings, so each is its own unit (I3), exactly as four options would be. Also no cut after لأن @173 or إلا بعد @316, tight subordinators sitting inside their stems.
